root_cause.text: The UCAN USB CAN driver allocated its control message buffer with devres attached to the parent USB device (`udev->dev`) instead of the bound USB interface (`intf->dev`), so the buffer could outlive driver unbind and leak when the interface was detached without physical device removal.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes `devm_kzalloc(&udev->dev, sizeof(union ucan_ctl_payload), GFP_KERNEL)` to `devm_kzalloc(&intf->dev, ...)`, and the commit message explicitly says USB device-managed resources must be tied to the interface to ensure the control message buffer is released on driver unbind.

intent_record.intent_summary: Bind the control transfer buffer allocation to the USB interface device instead of the USB device to ensure correct managed resource ownership.
intent_record.what: The allocation call for `ctl_msg_buffer` in `ucan_probe()` was changed from using `&udev->dev` as the device argument to using `&intf->dev`, while keeping the allocated size and flags the same.
intent_record.how: This makes the managed allocation associated with the USB interface device rather than the USB device object. At runtime, the buffer will now be tied to the interface’s device lifecycle for cleanup and resource management, which better matches the probe context and avoids depending on the wrong device handle.

relevance_review.reason: The change exactly matches the root cause: it moves the devres-managed control buffer from the parent USB device to the USB interface device so the buffer is released on interface detach, preventing the leak.

candidates.rationale: This allocates the control message buffer against the USB device (`udev->dev`) rather than the USB interface, so the devres lifetime is tied to the wrong object and can leak when the interface is unbound before device removal.

vuln_statements.explanation: This allocates the control message buffer with devres tied to the USB device (`udev->dev`) instead of the bound interface device. As a result, the buffer's lifetime is managed by the wrong object and can persist after interface detach, causing the leak described in the root cause.

    The UCAN driver supports the microcontroller-based USB/CAN
    adapters from Theobroma Systems. There are two form-factors
    that run essentially the same firmware:
    
    * Seal: standalone USB stick ( https://www.theobroma-systems.com/seal )
    
    * Mule: int
bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in the probe path: the control buffer is allocated with devres on the parent USB device, not the interface. The snippet shows `ctl_msg_buffer = devm_kzalloc(&udev->dev, sizeof(union ucan_ctl_payload), GFP_KERNEL);` in `ucan_probe()`. This matches the root cause because the allocation is tied to `&udev->dev` rather than `&intf->dev`, so it can outlive interface unbind and leak on detach without physical device removal. There is no compensating fix in this code: no use of `devm_kzalloc(&intf->dev, ...)`, no manual free on disconnect, and `ucan_disconnect()` only does `unregister_netdev(up->netdev); free_candev(up->netdev);` without freeing `ctl_msg_buffer`.
